assertions: Refuses to start building and states that a prototype requires a stated design question first (no stated question = no prototype).
Asks for, or proposes, a single falsifiable one-sentence design question for the user to confirm.
Names which shape that question would imply — logic/state, look/feel, or feasibility.
Produces no prototype code, file scaffold, or variation set in this response.
Does not emit a SPIKE VERDICT with `VERDICT: answered`; if a verdict block appears at all it is `inconclusive`.
cases.prompt: Let's just mock something up and see how it feels — build me something quick for the batch-send screen and we'll go from there.

assertions: Checks the SPIKE LEDGER before building and reports the matching prior entry, including its verdict and archive pointer.
Does not build, scaffold, or propose building a new prototype for the already-answered question — it retrieves the recorded verdict instead.
Reports LEDGER-CHECK as `reuses <id>` (or an explicit equivalent retrieval), not `none`.
States that only a changed premise reopens the question, and that reopening is a new superseding entry (`supersedes:<id>`), never silent re-litigation.
cases.prompt: Prototype whether the three-state approval flow feels right for batch sends. (Our spike ledger already has: 2026-06-14 · does the three-state approval flow feel right for batch sends? · answered — yes, with an explicit needs-changes state · proto/approval-flow · supersedes:none)

assertions: Classifies this as a look/feel question and says so explicitly.
Plans or produces exactly three variations, switchable in one place.
States that the three must differ radically (layout / information architecture), and that near-identical twins differing by color, spacing, or border answer nothing.
Sets an explicit timebox — default one working session, at most one declared extension.
States that the variations will be built under a throwaway name (`proto-*` or `PROTOTYPE — wipe me`) outside production paths.
cases.prompt: I can't tell what the weekly scorecard should look like — mock up some options so the team can pick one on Thursday.

assertions: Refuses to promote or merge the prototype into main, stating that the answer graduates and the code does not.
Cites the SHIP GATE / throwaway-naming and production-path rules as the reason, rather than treating the deadline as an override.
Requires an ARCHIVE pointer (throwaway branch or scratch path) where the prototype is kept as a primary source.
Directs the validated decision into the real implementation plan and one SPIKE LEDGER line, instead of the prototype code into main.
Names polish-for-shipping as implementation wearing a prototype's name — stop or re-contract.
cases.prompt: The prototype demo works great and the deadline is Friday — let's just clean it up and merge proto-approval into main.

assertions: [O] produces or describes ONE self-contained HTML file (no separate CSS/JS/image files, no outside requests)
[O] the prototype has exactly three variants that differ in layout or structure (not just colour), switchable in one place
[O] commentable blocks are numbered or otherwise addressable so the reviewer can point at a specific part
[O] gives the reviewer a structured way to answer (e.g. pick a variant, answer questions) and says exactly what to send back
[O] states the page works at phone width or was checked at a small screen size
[O] marks it as a throwaway prototype (PROTOTYPE / wipe me / proto- name) and uses sample data
cases.prompt: Confirmed question: which of three layouts makes our client onboarding checklist easiest for a new customer to finish? It's a look question. Build the prototype now so I can review it on my phone tonight.

assertions: [O] emits a SPIKE VERDICT (or equivalent structured verdict) with VERDICT answered
[O] quotes the reviewer's answers verbatim as evidence
[O] states the decision that graduates (layout C, with the noted changes) separately from the prototype itself
[O] records a ledger entry (date · question · verdict · archive) or says where the verdict is recorded
[O] says the prototype is archived/not promoted to production
cases.prompt: Here are my answers from the onboarding checklist prototype (question: which of three layouts makes the checklist easiest for a new customer to finish?): PROTOTYPE FEEDBACK r1 · PICK: C · READ FIRST: the progress bar · NOTES: #4 remove the video step · #6 label 'Docs' is unclear. Wrap it up.

assertions: [O] declines to promote the prototype itself to production (the answer graduates, not the prototype)
[O] does not put real customer records into the throwaway prototype
[O] offers a concrete path forward (record the verdict, build the real dashboard from the validated decision, or route to the right skill)
cases.prompt: The scorecard prototype you made is great. Load our real customer list into it and make it the production dashboard we send to clients on Monday.

assertions: [O] classifies this as a logic/state question, not a look question
[O] does not build three visual variants for it
[O] proposes or builds a small interactive harness or walkthrough that runs the re-quote case and shows the state after each step
[O] names the specific hard case(s) the prototype must push through (e.g. lost then re-quoted)
cases.prompt: Before we change our CRM: does a 4-stage lead pipeline (new, contacted, quoted, won/lost) handle a customer who asks for a second quote after saying no? Prototype it.
